resolutions.researcher_notes: No independent source attests this specific 8-inch Berri->Abu Ali gas line at all, let alone its operational status. All web hits for the value trace back to GEM (gem.wiki, excluded). Distinct sources cover the companion 'Abu Ali-Berri gas pipeline' (22 km/30 in, 2008) and the recent Saipem Berri Increment downstream crude/condensate lines (30 in/10 in, 2019-2023) - not this line. Both endpoints (Berri Gas Plant, Abu Ali GOSP) are long-operating Aramco facilities, which is only an indirect basis for 'operating'; left UNRESOLVED per the no-fabrication rule.

Fuel=Gas is GEM's classification of the line; no independent source describes this specific pipeline or what it carries. The Berri Gas Plant origin produces processed sales gas (see FuelSource ref), which is consistent with a gas line, but that supports the plant, not this pipe. UNRESOLVED - no source attests the pipeline itself.

CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: sheet has LengthKnown=39.00 km, but the source GEM wiki page itself states '37 km / 24 miles'. No independent source gives any length for this line. The seed cite (OPEC ASB 2012 p.75) is a statistical bulletin table and does not describe individual pipelines. UNRESOLVED; the 39 vs 37 km discrepancy should be reconciled by a human.
Diameter=8 in is GEM-only; no independent source states a diameter for this specific line. (Note the companion Abu Ali-Berri gas pipeline is 30 in - do not conflate.) UNRESOLVED.

Entity-level support for FuelSource='Berri Gas Plant'. Saudipedia: the Berri Gas Plant is a facility within Saudi Aramco's main gas network in al-Jubayl Industrial City, Eastern Province, that processes associated gas and supplies processed gas to the Jubail complex (verifier screen missed the 'Jubail' token due to JS rendering; content confirmed by page read). nsenergybusiness corroborates the Berri field's gas processing (370 Mscfd sour gas) under Aramco. These confirm the fuel source is a real Aramco gas plant, but neither states it feeds THIS specific line to Abu Ali - hence medium, not high.

Endpoint-level support. Start=Al Jubail/Eastern Province: Saudipedia places the Berri Gas Plant in al-Jubayl Industrial City, Eastern Province. End=Abu Ali Island/Eastern Province: nsenergybusiness describes the Abu Ali GOSP facility on the Berri field's eastern coast, ~50 km north of Ras Tanura, in the Jubail area. Both endpoints are confirmed real Aramco facilities in the Eastern Province. The route physically linking them is not directly attested by either source - medium.

Owner1='Saudi Aramco' 100%. nsenergybusiness: 'State-owned Saudi Aramco owns and operates the Berri field.' Saudipedia: the Berri Gas Plant is a Saudi Aramco facility. Both endpoints and the surrounding gas infrastructure are wholly Aramco, so Aramco ownership of a line between two of its own plants is strongly implied, but neither source names this pipeline explicitly - medium.
